text: This is not something you master overnight. But with practice, people can learn to distinguish openings, nearby obstacles, and even differences between certain shapes. Researchers have trained blind and sighted adults to echolocate over a period of ten weeks. And both groups improved. Now imagine what that learning process might feel like. A hallway is no longer simply an unknown stretch of space. You begin recognizing where a wall might end. Where an opening begins. Where there's enough room to move.
